items.title:
8.7K views · 56 reactions | Why Gold is Falling in War 2026

War usually pushes investors toward gold as a safe-haven asset so why is gold falling even while geopolitical tensions remain high?

In this video, I break down the key forces currently affecting gold prices and explain why war alone does not determine whether gold moves up or down.

One major factor is the attractiveness of US Treasury bonds. When bond yields remain high, investors may prefer assets that generate income instead of holding gold, which does not pay a yield. At the same time, rising oil prices can increase inflation expectations and influence future interest-rate decisions all of which can put additional pressure on gold.

We also discuss:

* Why gold normally performs well during uncertainty
* How US bond yields compete with gold
* The relationship between oil prices, inflation, and interest rates
* Why central banks continue accumulating gold
* How Middle East tensions could affect global markets
* What investors should watch in upcoming interest-rate decisions
* Why diversification matters in an unpredictable market
* How Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) can reduce timing risk

The most important point is that gold does not move because of one factor alone.

War, oil prices, inflation, bond yields, interest rates, central-bank demand, and global risk sentiment all interact with each other.

That is why trying to perfectly predict the next move in gold can be extremely difficult.

In uncertain markets, instead of putting a large amount into one asset at one price, investors may consider diversification and gradually investing over time according to their own financial situation and risk tolerance.

What do you think?

Will gold move higher from here, or could we see another decline?
